Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. I can see you're asking about three children: Alex, Blake, and Charlie.

Let me gather just a bit of information to make sure I have a complete picture:

1. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for any of these children?** (Only one person can claim Child Benefit per child)

2. **For Blake, who is 20 years old** - Can you confirm whether Blake is currently in any approved education or training? I understand they work 24+ hours per week, but I want to make sure about their education status.

3. **Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000?** (This won't affect eligibility, but it may mean you have to pay a tax charge)

These details will help me give you an accurate assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for each of your children.

## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

**Good news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **2 out of 3** of your children.

### Eligible Children:
✅ **Alex (age 7)** - You can claim Child Benefit for Alex even though they are fostered, because the local council is not paying for their accommodation or maintenance.

✅ **Charlie (age 7)** - You can claim Child Benefit for Charlie as they meet all the standard eligibility criteria (under 16, living with you, and you're responsible for them).

### Not Eligible:
❌ **Blake (age 20)** - Unfortunately, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake because they are working 24 hours or more per week and are not in approved education or training. Child Benefit stops when a child over 16 works 24+ hours per week outside of approved education.

### Next Steps:
If you're not already receiving Child Benefit for Alex and Charlie, you can make a claim for them. You would receive one payment covering both eligible children.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you would still be eligible to claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
